title: Divisibility multiplies
statement: For naturals a, b, c, e: if a divides b and c divides e then a*c divides b*e. The general law under pushing a pointwise divisibility through a product fold; the Nat prelude had Nat.dvd_mul, Nat.dvd_mul_right_of_dvd and Nat.dvd_trans but nothing multiplying two divisibilities.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.mul_dvd_mul : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : AxNat.dvd x0 x1) -> ((x5 : AxNat.dvd x2 x3) -> AxNat.dvd (AxNat.mul x0 x2) (AxNat.mul x1 x3)))))))

evidence.supports: Nat.mul_dvd_mul is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- Nat.mul_dvd_mul 2>/dev/null | grep -Fc '((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : AxNat.dvd x0 x1) -> ((x5 : AxNat.dvd x2 x3) -> AxNat.dvd (AxNat.mul x0 x2) (AxNat.mul x1 x3)))))))')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: The pattern is the FULL admitted type as rendered by Kernel::render_lean, not the theorem's name, so a drifted statement fails this check. Two Exists-eliminations on the divisibility hypotheses, then the witness is the product of the two cofactors and the equation is the four-factor rearrangement (a*u)*(c*v) = (a*c)*(u*v) -- three mul_assoc and one mul_comm, the same shape Nat.prodRange_mul's successor step uses.
